entries.originalText: “My Son, lose thyself and thou shalt find Me.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, lose yourself and you will find Me.

entries.originalText: Stand still without all choosing and all thought of self, and thou shalt ever be a gainer.
entries.modernizedText: Stand still without all choosing and all thought of self, and you will ever be a gainer.

entries.originalText: For more grace shall be added to thee, as soon as thou resignest thyself, and so long as thou dost not turn back to take thyself again.”
entries.modernizedText: For more grace will be added to you as soon as you resign yourself, and so long as you do not turn back to take yourself again.”

entries.originalText: O Lord, how often shall I resign myself, and in what things shall I lose myself?
entries.modernizedText: O Lord, how often shall I resign myself, and in what things shall I lose myself?

entries.originalText: “Always; every hour: in that which is little, and in that which is great.
entries.modernizedText: “Always; every hour: in that which is little, and in that which is great.

entries.originalText: I make no exception, but will that thou be found naked in all things.
entries.modernizedText: I make no exception, but will that you be found naked in all things.

entries.originalText: Otherwise how canst thou be Mine and I thine, unless thou be inwardly and outwardly free from every will of thine own?
entries.modernizedText: Otherwise how can you be Mine and I yours, unless you are inwardly and outwardly free from every will of your own?

entries.originalText: The sooner thou dost this, the better shall it be with thee; and the more fully and sincerely, the more thou shalt please Me, and the more abundantly shalt thou be rewarded.
entries.modernizedText: The sooner you do this, the better it will be with you; and the more fully and sincerely, the more you will please Me, and the more abundantly you will be rewarded.

entries.originalText: “Some resign themselves, but with certain reservations, for they do not fully trust in God, therefore they think that they have some provision to make for themselves.
entries.modernizedText: “Some resign themselves, but with certain reservations, for they do not fully trust in God; therefore they think that they have some provision to make for themselves.

entries.originalText: Some again at first offer everything; but afterwards being pressed by temptation they return to their own devices, and thus make no progress in virtue.
entries.modernizedText: Some again at first offer everything; but afterwards, being pressed by temptation, they return to their own devices, and thus make no progress in virtue.

entries.originalText: They will not attain to the true liberty of a pure heart, nor to the grace of My sweet companionship, unless they first entirely resign themselves and daily offer themselves up as a sacrifice; without this the union which bringeth forth fruit standeth not nor will stand.
entries.modernizedText: They will not attain the true liberty of a pure heart, or the grace of My sweet companionship, unless they first entirely resign themselves and daily offer themselves up as a sacrifice; without this the union which brings forth fruit does not stand and will not stand.

entries.originalText: “Many a time I have said unto thee, and now say again, Give thyself up, resign thyself, and thou shalt have great inward peace.
entries.modernizedText: “Many a time I have said to you, and now say again, Give yourself up, resign yourself, and you will have great inward peace.

entries.originalText: Give all for all; demand nothing, ask nothing in return; stand simply and with no hesitation in Me, and thou shalt possess Me.
entries.modernizedText: Give all for all; demand nothing, ask nothing in return; stand simply and with no hesitation in Me, and you will possess Me.

entries.originalText: Thou shalt have liberty of heart, and the darkness shall not overwhelm thee.
entries.modernizedText: You will have liberty of heart, and the darkness will not overwhelm you.

entries.originalText: For this strive thou, pray for it, long after it, that thou mayest be delivered from all possession of thyself, and nakedly follow Jesus who was made naked for thee; mayest die unto thyself and live eternally to Me.
entries.modernizedText: For this strive, pray for it, long after it, that you may be delivered from all possession of yourself, and nakedly follow Jesus who was made naked for you; may die to yourself and live eternally to Me.

entries.originalText: Then shall all vain fancies disappear, all evil disturbings, and superfluous cares.
entries.modernizedText: Then all vain fancies will disappear, all evil disturbances, and unnecessary cares.

entries.originalText: Then also shall immoderate fear depart from thee, and inordinate love shall die.”
entries.modernizedText: Then also immoderate fear will depart from you, and inordinate love will die.”
